entries.title: Leviticus 7:7
segments: Shall have it; that portion of it which was not burnt on the altar.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:10
segments: While God requires his ministers to devote their time and talents to his immediate service, he also requires that their temporal wants be supplied by those for whose spiritual good they labor.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:13
segments: Leavened bread; that which was offered to the Lord was to be unleavened, as before prescribed,
; but that which the priest ate himself, in token of thanksgiving for mercies, might, like common bread, be leavened.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:15
segments: The same day that it is offered; this was probably to prevent its being reserved by the offerer for his private use.  He had devoted it to Jehovah, and now it was no longer his own.  Of it he was to make a feast for his friends, and especially for the poor of his people.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:16
segments:
A vow; a sacrifice offered upon the paying of a vow.  The flesh of this, and of the voluntary offering, might be eaten the second day; but what remained till the third day was to be burnt with fire.  In those warm regions it is difficult to keep flesh over the second day in perfect purity, which may have been one reason for this injunction. 
 
While we are called to mourning on account of our sins, we are also called to rejoicing on account of the goodness of God; and our joy may sometimes be appropriately express by feasting on the bounties of his providence and grace.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:18
segments:
It; his offering.  If he ate any of the flesh after the second day, his offering would be rejected. 
 
  Bear his iniquity; be held guilty, and exposed to punishment.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:23
segments: No manner of fat; of that fat of beasts which was to be offered in sacrifice to God.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:26
segments: No manner of blood; that which flows from the arteries and veins, called the life, or the blood of the life.  The blood which mingled with the flesh when cooked, was not forbidden.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:30
segments: Each individual, while he relies on the great atonement for salvation, must also himself be voluntary and active in presenting his offerings to God, and in doing what he requires.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:34
segments: Wave-breast--heave-shoulder; that had been consecrated to Jehovah by waving and heaving.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:35
segments: The portion of the anointing of Aaron; his portion in consequence of his having been anointed as high-priest.
